test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On: 25 May 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: How is tuberculosis spread in humans?
solution:
The correct option is__** Droplet Infection.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB)** is an infectious disease usually caused by the** Bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis**.
 
• **Robert Koch** received **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1905** for the discover of the bacteria causing TB.
 
• The only available vaccine as of 2021 is** Bacillus Calmette-Guérin** commonly known as BCG.
 
• Intradermal** MVA85A** vaccine in addition to BCG injection is not effective in preventing tuberculosis.
 
• **The World Health Organization (WHO)** declared TB a **"global health emergency"** in **1993**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• TB is an airborne disease (diseases that spread through air). Another example of such disease is Covid-19.
 
• In 2020, an estimated 10 million people developed active TB, resulting in 1.5 million deaths, making TB the** second leading cause of death** from an infectious disease after COVID-19.
 
• More than 50% of cases being diagnosed in seven countries:
 
 
• **India (27%)**
 
• **China (9%)**
 
• **Indonesia (8%)**
 
• **Philippines (6%)**
 
• **Pakistan (6%)**
 
• **Nigeria (4%)**
 
• **Bangladesh (4%) **
 
 
 
• **Dr. Harshvardhan, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare **launched the new **TB Harega Desh Jeetega Campaign**.
